title.narrative: The Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy, and Accountability Kenya - PW1

description.narrative: The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.The main objective of pathway 1 is to strengthen the advocacy capacity of 9 women’s rights organizations (WROs) to amplify young women’s voices in Kenya by 2025. As specific objectives this pathway envisages amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organizations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. Also, by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies. KIT, Equality Now and the Country Leads facilitate capacity strengthening. KIT is responsible for the design and implementation of the WROs advocacy and organizational capacity assessment, the design of the individual WRO/FBO capacity development plans, and a collective learning agenda as well as the facilitation of reflective monitoring and adaptive learning approaches with the WROs.

title.narrative: IO1 Enhanced capacity of 16-28 WROs to amplify young women's voices

description.narrative: Under IO1, YW4A focuses on enhancing the organizational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organizations (WROs) in each programme country through providing capacity building training and involving them in advocacy activities. The programme strives that these WROs will be amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organizations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. Also, by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies identified under IO4.

title.narrative: # of WROs with enhanced capacity on the AOCA scale to advance young women’s rights to bodily integrity and equal participation in decision-making.

description.narrative: In order to assess the advocacy and organizational capacity of the WROs, KIT designed the Advocacy and Organizational Capacity Assessment (AOCA) method measuring 21 different sub-domains. These sub-domains concern a selected number of capacities that are considered instrumental for WROs to efficiently and successfully carry out their advocacy activities, and to involve and amplify young women's voices. The assessment results in the AOCA measure and category, an ordinal scale, which indicates a WROs current advocacy and organizational capacity level to amplify young women’s voices and promote young women’s leadership and equal participation in (political) decision-making, their bodily integrity, and the prevention and elimination of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). This score represents the baseline value for IO1. There are seven different categories reflecting the WROs capacity level: 1. Well-developed (score 11 or higher) 2. Good (between 9 and 10.9) 3. Moderate (between 7 and 8.9) 4. Fair (between 5 and 6.9) 5. Basic (between 3 and 4.9) 6. Limited (between 1 and 2.9) 7. Very limited (lower than 0.9).Since we are not able to present ordinal scale in IATI, we are presenting the baseline values of the WROs in the respective countries as a unit, indicating the baseline in all countries to be at zero as in 2021 the AOCA level was measured. The target set reflects the number of WROs who have moved one level up on the AOCA scale, rather than the actual AOCA scales.

comment.narrative: In Kenya YW4A targets 9 WROs under IO1. In Y1 the advocacy and organisational capacity of the participating WROs was measured, as to set the baseline situation. In Kenya the WROs baseline AOCA capacity level is assessed as follows: 1 WRO at GOOD capacity (WRG048); 2 WROs at MODERATE capacity (WRG048, WRG045); 3 WROs at BASIC capacity (1 WRG045; 2 WRG048); 2 WROs at LIMITED capacity (both WRG047).One of the WROs was not yet active at the time of AOCA assessment, hence this organization's baseline will be measured at a later stage.Additions as of mid-term: In Kenya the baseline AOCA capacity level of the WRO that became active after baseline study is assessed at BASIC capacity. And the new WRO that joined in 2023 is assessed at FAIR capacity (replacing a WRO with GOOD capacity).

By the end of Y5, it is expected that in total 20 WROs in all four participating countries have moved one level up or more on the 7-point AOCA measure scale compared to baseline (80% of the WROs that participated in baseline study). For Kenya we expect that 7 WROs have increased their AOCA measure with at least one level.

By the end of Y5, it is expected that in total 20 WROs in all four participating countries have moved one level up or more on the 7-point AOCA measure scale compared to baseline (80% of the WROs that participated in baseline study). For Kenya we expect that 7 WROs have increased their AOCA measure with at least one level.

YW4A intends to work with the same 27 WROs throughout the programme duration across the four countries. At mid-term, an AOCA-reassessment workshop was conducted with a total of 7 WROs in Kenya, those organisations who were involved in YW4A since the start, to capture potential changes in WRO capacity and quantitative AOCA measures compared to baseline. The results from the AOCA mid-term assessment indicate progress among all seven WROs compared to their baseline AOCA. A total of six WROs moved up one level on the AOCA scale, and while one WRO enhanced its AOCA measure compared to baseline, it still fell within the same capacity category. Resulting in the following mid-term levels: 2 WROs at BASIC capacity, 3 WROs with FAIR capacity, 1 WRO at MODERATE and 1 WRO at GOOD capacity. Hence in Kenya, 86% of the WROs that joined YW4A since 2021 have met YW4A’s IO1 target to move up one level on the AOCA scale.The re-assessment showed that there was a steady increase in WRO’s capacity in all four AOCA main domains. The highest capacity increase is visible in the domain commitment to young women’s voices, while for some organisations applying an intersectional lens to diversify the group of young women reached by YW4A was still a challenge. The WROs tactical and strategic advocacy skills have increased resulting from the social media and legal advocacy trainings led by partner Equality Now.
